backup.production_rule: Pay ahead: staff_pay_requests.lines may now hold kind 'advance' lines {checkout_date, date, type turnover, base, transport, amount, guest} for a checkout that has no report yet (get_missed_cleanings, 30 days), made only through the new staff_pay_admin_create_v2(payee, sessions, claim_ids, advance, key) (reasons advance_not_owed, advance_taken; the 20-line cap counts them); staff_pay_admin_create_v1 is now a wrapper passing no advance lines. staff_pay_settle_v1 writes one expense row per advance line (external_ref cleanadv:<request>:<date>, idempotent on the ref), refuses a line of an unknown kind (bad_line) instead of paying it as a claim, and sets logged_by to the actor whenever no Telegram id is given. A new AFTER INSERT trigger on cleaning_sessions (cleaning_sessions_link_advance, definer, never fails the insert) joins a later report by the payee to the request that paid its checkout ahead and stamps it paid when the request is paid. staff_pay_candidates_v1 adds reports_owed, staff_pay_admin_list_v1 adds advance_candidates and the line guest, staff_pay_notice_v1 adds reports_owed (ISO dates). get_meter_photo_followups drops sessions with fee_paid_at set. New table meter_photo_prechecks (RLS on, service_role only). Cron verify-meter-photo-daily moves from 30 23 * * * to */10 * * * * (name and command unchanged) and job_heartbeats.expected_interval_seconds from 86400 to 600. Replaced bodies are the live ones of 2026-10-20 plus only these edits (guarded on their md5). The Honey 3,250 data step (supabase/sql/2026-10-20-s94-honey-3250.sql) runs AFTER this applies.
backup.notes: Additive: one new table, two new functions and one trigger, one wrapper and five replaced function bodies (guarded on the live md5), one cron schedule and one heartbeat interval. Old apps keep working: no key was removed from any payload and old clients never send advance lines. Deploy order: SQL, then the waves function verify-meter-photo (precheck mode and the cache), then the Staff app. Then run the Honey data step.
